branch 'main' set up to track 'origin/main'.
> **Milestone:** M2. **Status:** draft for review. M5's version will carry a
> changelog of what this one got wrong.
> Macy travels about three nights a month and leaves a laptop, cash, and bags in
> a hotel room all day. Our device sits in the room while she is out and, when
> she returns, answers one question with a short timeline: *did anyone come in,
> when, and for how long?* It has no internet connection, no cloud, and no
> account; every byte stays on its SD card. Macy reads the timeline from her
> phone over the device's own Wi-Fi hotspot.
> 
> **The narrowed claim:** in a test room, the device separates *door-entry
> events* (motion plus a door/voice sound signature) from *motion-only* and
> *sound-only* events with a measured confusion matrix, and keeps a
> crash-consistent record of them through power cuts and sensor faults.
> 
> **Mechanisms:** **B** interrupt-driven GPIO input (PIR and arm button) vs.
> polling; **D** a crash-consistent storage layer; **E** multi-process
> supervision.
> 
> **Hardware:** Raspberry Pi 5 with RTC backup battery · HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO,
> keyed connector) · Blue Snowball USB microphone (ALSA) · Arducam OV5647 (CSI,
> Pi 5 22-pin cable) · arm button + LED (GPIO). PIR and microphone are the two
> *cooperating* sensors; the camera only collects evidence for confirmed entries.
>  PIR + button (GPIO)    Blue Snowball (USB)        OV5647 (CSI)
>      | GPIO edges           | USB isoc audio           | CSI-2
> =====|======================|==========================|===================== kernel
>  RP1 gpiochip            snd-usb-audio             libcamera
>  (kernel timestamps)     (44.1 kHz s16 = 88.2 KB/s)
> =====|======================|==========================|===================== user
>      v                      v                          v
>  +--------+           +-----------+             +-----------+
>  |  pird  |           |   micd    |             |   camd    |
>  | PIR +  |           | 20 ms FFT |             | burst on  |
>  | button |           | features; |             | trigger,  |
>  | + LED  |           | 15 s PCM  |             | ~2 fps    |
>  +--------+           | ring      |             +-----------+
>      | edge/button    +-----------+   trigger (<1/min) ^  | frame-ready
>      | msgs <1 Hz,          | features 50 Hz x 64 B    |  | 2 Hz, path only
>      | ~40 B                | = 3.2 KB/s               |  v
>  +--------------------------------------------------------------+
>  |                     hub (single writer)                      |
>  |  analysis/: background model -> detectors -> fusion FSM      |
>  |  store/: event log + stats log (append, CRC) + clip store    |
>  |  arm state machine; query socket                             |
>  +--------------------------------------------------------------+
>      | events ~0.1-20/hr (fsync on open and close); clips ~6-9 MB
>      | per confirmed entry; stats 1/min batched
>  SD card: /var/lib/pss/{events/, stats/, clips/}
>  supervisor (E): fork/execs pird, micd, camd, hub, ui; 5 s heartbeats from
>  each over AF_UNIX; hourly soak heartbeat (liveness, RSS, fds, counts).
>  Macy's phone --Wi-Fi (hotspot, no uplink)--> ui (read-only page) --AF_UNIX--> hub
>  pss (CLI, over SSH on the hotspot) --AF_UNIX query socket (~1/min)--> hub
> All internal IPC is AF_UNIX `SOCK_SEQPACKET`: message boundaries are kept, and
> a dead peer shows up as EOF/EPIPE, which is the fault signal E needs.
> | Process | Threads | Inputs → outputs |
> |---|---|---|
> | `supervisor` | 1 (epoll: signalfd, child sockets, timerfd) | heartbeats → restarts, soak log |
> | `pird` | 1 (blocks on GPIO edge events, or `timerfd` in poll mode) | PIR/button edges → msgs; LED |
> | `micd` | 2: ALSA capture + feature thread, joined by an SPSC ring | PCM → features; audio clip on request |
> | `camd` | 1 + `rpicam-still` child per burst | trigger → JPEGs in `clips/*.tmp` |
> | `hub` | 1 (epoll over child + query sockets, timerfd) | features + edges → events, storage |
> | `ui` | 1 (Python, `ui/`, display only) | HTTP on hotspot address → hub queries |
> 
> All run at default priority; mechanism C is not claimed.
> ### B: Interrupt-driven GPIO input (`pird`, `src/capture/pir`)
> **Implementation.** `pird` requests the PIR and button lines through libgpiod
> v2 with both edges and kernel timestamps (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), and blocks until
> the RP1 GPIO interrupt delivers an edge. A `--poll=<ms>` mode reads line values
> on a `timerfd` instead; that is the comparison arm.
> **Why Macy needs it.** The device sits idle for hours and must catch the few
> edges that matter. An interrupt reports every edge with the kernel's
> timestamp; a poll only knows a change happened somewhere in the last interval,
> and can miss a button press shorter than that interval entirely. A 10 ms poll
> also wakes the CPU 100 times a second for a sensor that changes a few times a
> day. We are honest about scale: the PIR itself takes hundreds of milliseconds
> to react to motion, and on a Pi 5 the CPU difference may be small. We will
> report whatever we measure.
> **Measured.** Edge-to-userspace latency distribution, missed short pulses, and
> `pird` CPU, IRQ vs. poll at 1, 10, 100 ms, idle and under load (Section 9).
> 
> ### D: Crash-consistent storage (`src/store`, linked into `hub`)
> **Implementation.** Append-only CRC32-framed logs in segment files (events and
> stats kept separately); atomic clip commits (tmp → fsync → rename → fsync dir);
> recovery at startup; byte quota with oldest-first clip eviction (Section 5).
> **Why Macy needs it.** The device runs from a hotel wall outlet, and outlets
> get used: housekeeping unplugs things to vacuum, Macy unplugs it to pack, and
> an intruder may pull the plug on purpose. The record exists to answer "did
> someone come in?" after the fact, so it must survive exactly that.
> **Measured.** Power-pull recovery (records lost, corrupt records accepted,
> dangling clip references), bytes written per day, fsync count and latency.
> 
> ### E: Multi-process supervision (`src/supervisor`)
> **Implementation.** One process per sensor, plus hub, ui, and supervisor.
> Children heartbeat every 5 s. The supervisor restarts any child that exits or
> misses heartbeats for 15 s (SIGKILL first), with backoff 1 s → 60 s that resets
> after 10 min healthy. Exit code `3` means "device gone": the supervisor retries
> every 30 s and the hub marks that sensor DEGRADED instead of storming restarts.
> **Why Macy needs it.** A security monitor that silently dies is worse than
> none, because Macy believes it is on duty. If the camera hangs or the mic drops
> off USB, the PIR record must keep flowing and the timeline must say which
> sensors were offline and when.
> **Measured.** `kill -9` each child and unplug the mic: detection time, recovery
> time, events lost during the gap, log excerpts.
> spectral flux. FFT is a primitive (small library or our own radix-2).
> **Background model.** Per band, an exponentially weighted mean and variance
> (time constant ~60 s), updated only outside active events so a conversation
> doesn't become "background". Frames are scored as per-band z-scores, so the
> same device works next to a loud HVAC unit and in a silent room.
> - *Impulse (latch/door):* spectral-flux z-score above `K_imp`, broadband, decay
>   under 150 ms.
> - *Voice:* z-score in the 300–3400 Hz bands above `K_voice` for ≥ 400 ms within
>   2 s, with sub-200 Hz energy not dominant (rules out HVAC).
> - *PIR:* HC-SR501 in **single-trigger mode** with the delay pot at minimum, so
>   each detection is a pulse of a few seconds followed by a ~2.5 s low block
>   time, even under continuous motion. A person moving around produces a train
>   of pulses.
> IDLE --PIR rise--> MOTION_WINDOW (±T_co = 3 s around the edge; audio history checked)
> MOTION_WINDOW --impulse or voice in window--> ENTRY (confirmed; durable at once)
> IDLE --impulse/voice, no PIR within ±T_co--> SOUND_ONLY (hallway)
> ENTRY/MOTION_ONLY --no PIR pulse and no voice for T_quiet = 30 s--> close event
> ```

content.text:
I stopped before pushing anything to `main`. GitHub is unchanged, your work is safe on `m3-pipeline`, and I reset your local `main` to match GitHub's.

Owen pushed two commits to `main` on Oct 20 that change things, and two of the changes matter more than a merge conflict.

### 1. The new CLAUDE.md gives the capture daemons to Owen
> - Owen: capture daemons and arm button (`src/capture/{pir,mic,cam}`)
> - Bryan: storage layer, analysis engine (`src/store`, `src/analysis`)
> - Each partner works in their own clone and their own Claude Code sessions

In your session I wrote `pird`, `camd` and `micd`, which are now Owen's area. DESIGN.md says ownership means "first authorship and answerability at the defense." Putting your session's capture code on `main` could cause a grading problem for both of you. **Owen should decide this, not just you and me.**

### 2. The design changed, and part of the code no longer matches it
- **Storage (your area):** separate `events/` and `stats/` logs instead of one `log/`, and an event is made durable when it **opens**, not just when it closes.
- **`pird` (Owen's area):** must also handle an arm button and LED.
- **Hub (shared):** needs an arm/disarm state machine.
- **Other changes:** the mic ring is 15 s instead of ~12 s. `Design.md` was renamed `DESIGN.md`, so M3-Status.md links to a file that no longer exists.
- **Already compatible:** the new `netcheck` rule allows network code only in the hotspot UI under `ui/`. The existing check only scans `src/`, so it's fine.

### What I'd suggest
1. **Talk to Owen first.** Either Owen keeps the capture daemons as a starting point and reviews them, or Owen writes their own and you drop yours. I'd remove `src/capture/` from your branch unless Owen explicitly says to keep it.
2. **Then I update your part to the new DESIGN.md:** the events/stats split and fsync on open in `src/store`, plus fixing the references. With your OK, I'd also update the hub, since it's shared.
3. **Then rebase onto Owen's `main`.** No files overlap, so it should go cleanly. Push to `main` after the tests pass.

What did Owen say about the capture code, or should I hold until you've talked?

# Portable Security System: team rules

## Commands
- Build: `make`    Cross/deploy: `make deploy PI=pi@<host>`
- Tests: `make test`    Sanitizers: `make asan`    Valgrind: `make memcheck`
- Network boundary check: `make netcheck` (fails if network code appears
  outside the hotspot UI server; see DESIGN.md Section 11)
- Soak sanity: `make soakcheck` (1-hour miniature of the 48h run)
- A change is DONE only when build, test, asan, and netcheck pass. Show output.

## Hard constraints
- The PRODUCT makes no network calls. Its only network code is the
  local UI server, bound to the Pi's own hotspot address (no internet
  uplink, no outbound connections). No LLM APIs, no cloud inference,
  no pretrained models. The intelligence in src/analysis is ours.
  This is a graded boundary.
- Every daemon must be supervisable: clean exit codes, no orphaned
  fds across restart, heartbeat within 60s of start.
- Every allocation checked; every syscall's error path handled and
  logged. The 48-hour soak is the test suite of last resort.
- NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.

## Project facts (see DESIGN.md)
- Pi 5, wall powered (no battery). RTC backup battery is required: wall
  time across power cuts depends on it.
- Sensors: HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO), Blue Snowball USB mic (ALSA), OV5647
  camera (CSI, evidence only), arm button + LED (GPIO).
- Safe to hot-unplug for fault injection: the USB mic. The PIR only via
  its keyed connector. NEVER hot-unplug the CSI camera ribbon.

## Ownership
- Owen: capture daemons and arm button (src/capture/{pir,mic,cam})
- Bryan: storage layer, analysis engine (src/store, src/analysis)
- Shared: hub, supervisor, CLI, UI (src/hub, src/supervisor, src/cli, ui/)
- Each partner works in their own clone and their own Claude Code
  sessions; never prompt jointly in one session. Copy transcripts to
  CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/<name>/ at every milestone.
- The agent edits outside the session owner's area only when told
  explicitly to.

## Style
- Systems core: C17, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, no VLAs.
  goto-cleanup for multi-resource functions.
- Python permitted only under tools/ and ui/. No graded mechanism
  may live there.
- Smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.

## Workflow
- Multi-file or algorithmic change: plan first, wait for approval.
- Hardware bugs: paste real evidence (dmesg, timing capture,
  /proc/interrupts). No fixes proposed from a verbal description.
- Commit only from a green state; message format "M<n>: <what>".

content.text:
All three results are good:
- **libgpiod 2.2.1** is new enough for `pird`.
- **The camera works.**
- **`make test` passes on the Pi**, so the code builds and runs on the real hardware.

And yes, the PIR needs wires. Here's how to connect it.

### What you need
**3 female-to-female jumper wires** (the "Dupont" kind with a socket on both ends). They fit straight onto the PIR's pins and the Pi's header pins. If your kit has a keyed PIR connector, that works too.

### 1. Shut the Pi down first
```
sudo poweroff
```
Wait for the green light to stop blinking, then **unplug the power**. Never wire with the Pi on.

### 2. Find the PIR's pins
Pull the white dome off the HC-SR501 gently; it just pops off. Next to the 3 pins you'll see labels: **VCC**, **OUT**, **GND**. The order varies between boards, so trust the labels.

### 3. Connect the wires
The Pi's 40-pin header is numbered with **physical pin numbers**. Pin 1 is the corner pin nearest the SD card slot, odd numbers run along the inner row and even numbers along the outer edge.

| PIR pin | → | Pi physical pin | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| **VCC** | → | **pin 2** | 5V power |
| **GND** | → | **pin 6** | Ground |
| **OUT** | → | **pin 11** | GPIO17 (the code's default) |

The PIR runs on 5V, but its OUT signal is 3.3V, so it's safe to connect directly to the Pi. **Double-check VCC and GND before powering on:** swapping them can damage the sensor.

### 4. Set the PIR's controls (DESIGN.md says how)
- **Jumper:** set it to **single-trigger** (usually marked **L**).
- **Time-delay knob** (usually labeled Tx or "time"): turn it fully **counterclockwise** to the minimum.
- **Sensitivity knob:** leave it in the middle.

Put the dome back on.

### 5. Power on and test the wiring alone
Plug the Pi back in and open the Terminal. Then:
```
gpioinfo GPIO17
```
This should print a line mentioning `GPIO17`. Then:
```
gpiomon GPIO17
```
**Wait about 60 seconds without moving in front of it**; the PIR is warming up and may fire randomly. Then wave your hand in front of it. You should see `rising` and `falling` lines appear. Press **Ctrl-C** to stop.

### Tell me
1. What `gpioinfo GPIO17` printed (just the chip name, like `gpiochip0` or `gpiochip4`)
2. Did `gpiomon` show `rising`/`falling` lines when you waved? (yes/no)

If both work, the next step is running our actual `hub` + `pird` with the PIR.

content.content:
**Fusion state machine (in `hub`).**
```
IDLE --PIR rise--> MOTION_WINDOW (±T_co = 3 s around the edge; audio history checked)
MOTION_WINDOW --impulse or voice in window--> ENTRY (confirmed; durable at once)
MOTION_WINDOW --window expires, no audio--> MOTION_ONLY
IDLE --impulse/voice, no PIR within ±T_co--> SOUND_ONLY (hallway)
ENTRY/MOTION_ONLY --no PIR pulse and no voice for T_quiet = 30 s--> close event
```
Opening and closing use different conditions, so ten minutes of someone moving
around is one event, not forty.

**Arm state machine (in `hub`, button handled by `pird`).**
```
DISARMED --button--> EXIT_DELAY (60 s, LED blinks) --> ARMED (LED off)
ARMED --ENTRY confirmed--> GRACE (30 s) --button--> DISARMED, entry labelled `owner`
GRACE --30 s, no button--> ARMED, entry reported (routine / UNEXPECTED)
```
Events are only reported while ARMED. Macy can also use `pss arm` /
`pss disarm`. The LED stays dark while armed so the device doesn't draw
attention.

**Routine vs. unexpected (optional).** Housekeeping times are often unknown,
so the expected window is optional (`pss expect 10:00-14:00`). With no window,
every confirmed entry while armed is reported plainly; with one, entries
inside it are labelled `routine` and others `UNEXPECTED`. The device never
tries to identify who entered.

**Why a threshold cannot do this.** A loudness threshold fires on every
hallway door slam and misses a quiet entry in a noisy room; a PIR alone fires
on curtains moved by HVAC. The decision rests on the *timing* of two different
physical signals, scored against a background learned in *this* room, with
hysteresis on event boundaries. No single `if` reproduces that.

## 5. Storage and data

| Data | Rate | Format | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event records | ~0.1–20/hr | `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]` | kept (tiny); never evicted |
| Stats / heartbeat records | 1/min, batched | same framing, separate segments | whole segments deleted after 7 days |
| Audio clips (confirmed entries) | 10 s pre-roll + ≤ 20 s post ≈ 2.6 MB | WAV | clip quota, oldest first |
| Image bursts (confirmed entries) | ~2 fps × 10 s ≈ 3–6 MB | JPEG | clip quota, oldest first |
| Daemon text logs | low | timestamped lines | logrotate, 4 × 5 MB |

**Event log.** Segments `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel`, capped at 4 MB. When an ENTRY
is confirmed, an `event_open` record is appended and `fdatasync`ed
immediately; `event_close` is synced when the event ends. So if someone pulls
the plug mid-entry, the entry is already on disk. Recovery turns an open
without a close into an event marked `interrupted (power lost)`.
MOTION_ONLY and SOUND_ONLY events are written once, at close.

**Stats log.** Separate segments in `stats/`, buffered in memory and flushed
once a minute. A power cut loses at most a minute of stats, never an event.
Because stats live apart from events, old stats are dropped by deleting whole
segments, with no compaction.

**Clips.** Written as `clips/<event-id>.{wav,dir}.tmp`; on completion: fsync
file → rename → fsync directory. The record referencing a clip is written only
after the rename is durable, so the log never points at a missing clip. Bursts
for unconfirmed events are deleted. The `micd` PCM ring holds 15 s, so a full
10 s pre-roll still exists after the ~3 s confirmation delay.

**Recovery (hub start).** For the newest event and stats segments: stop at the
first bad length or CRC, `ftruncate` there, and log `store: recovered seg=N
valid=R truncated_bytes=B`. Delete every `clips/*.tmp` and log each. Close any
open entry as `interrupted`. Rebuild the in-memory index.

**Power-loss gaps.** The hub writes a `boot` record at every start. The gap
between the last durable stats record and `boot` is when the device was off,
accurate to about a minute; the timeline shows it as `OFFLINE` so Macy doesn't
read silence as "nobody came in".

**Quota.** Default 2 GiB for `clips/` (~250 entries). Before each clip, evict
the oldest clips until there is room. Below a 5 % free-space floor, clips stop
and event records continue.

**Time.** There is no NTP offline. Wall time comes from the Pi 5's RTC, and the
RTC backup battery is a **requirement**: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` restarts at every
boot, so after a power cut only the RTC knows how long the device was off.
Records carry both clocks; intervals and ordering use monotonic time within a
boot. If the RTC reports an unset clock at boot, the hub logs it and the
timeline shows the gap as `OFFLINE (duration unknown)` until the clock is set
(`pss settime`, or the "set clock from this phone" button on the UI page).

## 6. Failure-mode table

| Component | Failure | Detected by | System response | Log shows |
|---|---|---|---|---|

toolUseResult.stdout:
**Fusion state machine (in `hub`).**
```
IDLE --PIR rise--> MOTION_WINDOW (±T_co = 3 s around the edge; audio history checked)
MOTION_WINDOW --impulse or voice in window--> ENTRY (confirmed; durable at once)
MOTION_WINDOW --window expires, no audio--> MOTION_ONLY
IDLE --impulse/voice, no PIR within ±T_co--> SOUND_ONLY (hallway)
ENTRY/MOTION_ONLY --no PIR pulse and no voice for T_quiet = 30 s--> close event
```
Opening and closing use different conditions, so ten minutes of someone moving
around is one event, not forty.

**Arm state machine (in `hub`, button handled by `pird`).**
```
DISARMED --button--> EXIT_DELAY (60 s, LED blinks) --> ARMED (LED off)
ARMED --ENTRY confirmed--> GRACE (30 s) --button--> DISARMED, entry labelled `owner`
GRACE --30 s, no button--> ARMED, entry reported (routine / UNEXPECTED)
```
Events are only reported while ARMED. Macy can also use `pss arm` /
`pss disarm`. The LED stays dark while armed so the device doesn't draw
attention.

**Routine vs. unexpected (optional).** Housekeeping times are often unknown,
so the expected window is optional (`pss expect 10:00-14:00`). With no window,
every confirmed entry while armed is reported plainly; with one, entries
inside it are labelled `routine` and others `UNEXPECTED`. The device never
tries to identify who entered.

**Why a threshold cannot do this.** A loudness threshold fires on every
hallway door slam and misses a quiet entry in a noisy room; a PIR alone fires
on curtains moved by HVAC. The decision rests on the *timing* of two different
physical signals, scored against a background learned in *this* room, with
hysteresis on event boundaries. No single `if` reproduces that.

## 5. Storage and data

| Data | Rate | Format | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event records | ~0.1–20/hr | `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]` | kept (tiny); never evicted |
| Stats / heartbeat records | 1/min, batched | same framing, separate segments | whole segments deleted after 7 days |
| Audio clips (confirmed entries) | 10 s pre-roll + ≤ 20 s post ≈ 2.6 MB | WAV | clip quota, oldest first |
| Image bursts (confirmed entries) | ~2 fps × 10 s ≈ 3–6 MB | JPEG | clip quota, oldest first |
| Daemon text logs | low | timestamped lines | logrotate, 4 × 5 MB |

**Event log.** Segments `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel`, capped at 4 MB. When an ENTRY
is confirmed, an `event_open` record is appended and `fdatasync`ed
immediately; `event_close` is synced when the event ends. So if someone pulls
the plug mid-entry, the entry is already on disk. Recovery turns an open
without a close into an event marked `interrupted (power lost)`.
MOTION_ONLY and SOUND_ONLY events are written once, at close.

**Stats log.** Separate segments in `stats/`, buffered in memory and flushed
once a minute. A power cut loses at most a minute of stats, never an event.
Because stats live apart from events, old stats are dropped by deleting whole
segments, with no compaction.

**Clips.** Written as `clips/<event-id>.{wav,dir}.tmp`; on completion: fsync
file → rename → fsync directory. The record referencing a clip is written only
after the rename is durable, so the log never points at a missing clip. Bursts
for unconfirmed events are deleted. The `micd` PCM ring holds 15 s, so a full
10 s pre-roll still exists after the ~3 s confirmation delay.

**Recovery (hub start).** For the newest event and stats segments: stop at the
first bad length or CRC, `ftruncate` there, and log `store: recovered seg=N
valid=R truncated_bytes=B`. Delete every `clips/*.tmp` and log each. Close any
open entry as `interrupted`. Rebuild the in-memory index.

**Power-loss gaps.** The hub writes a `boot` record at every start. The gap
between the last durable stats record and `boot` is when the device was off,
accurate to about a minute; the timeline shows it as `OFFLINE` so Macy doesn't
read silence as "nobody came in".

**Quota.** Default 2 GiB for `clips/` (~250 entries). Before each clip, evict
the oldest clips until there is room. Below a 5 % free-space floor, clips stop
and event records continue.

**Time.** There is no NTP offline. Wall time comes from the Pi 5's RTC, and the
RTC backup battery is a **requirement**: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` restarts at every
boot, so after a power cut only the RTC knows how long the device was off.
Records carry both clocks; intervals and ordering use monotonic time within a
boot. If the RTC reports an unset clock at boot, the hub logs it and the
timeline shows the gap as `OFFLINE (duration unknown)` until the clock is set
(`pss settime`, or the "set clock from this phone" button on the UI page).

# Plan: bring src/store in line with Owen's updated DESIGN.md §5

## Context
M3 code is on `main` (3e87ee9). Owen's M2 revision (6fd043f) changed the
storage design after our store was written. Hardware testing is blocked
(no PIR jumper wires), so we use the time on Bryan's own area, `src/store`,
so it matches what graders will compare against. Session owner: Bryan.
`src/hub` and `src/cli` are shared; they get only the call-site changes the
new store API forces (covered by approving this plan).

What DESIGN.md §5 now requires that we don't do:
1. **Two logs:** `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel` and `stats/seg-NNNNNN.pel` (4 MB
   segments each, same framing), not one `log/`. Layout `{events, stats, clips}`.
2. **ENTRY durable at open:** `event_open` record + `fdatasync` when an ENTRY is
   confirmed; close record synced at end. MOTION_ONLY / SOUND_ONLY are written
   once, at close (what the hub does today, so M3 behavior is unchanged).
3. **Recovery closes dangling opens** as `interrupted (power lost)`.
4. **Stats retention:** whole stats segments deleted after 7 days.
5. Recovery truncates the newest segment of **both** logs.

## Design
- **`src/store/evlog.{c,h}`** becomes a generic segment log plus the store:
  - `struct seglog { int dir_fd, seg_fd; uint32_t seg_no; uint64_t seg_size; uint8_t buf[...]; }`
    with `seglog_append()` / `seglog_sync()`: the current append/rollover/
    truncate-on-failed-write code moved, not rewritten.
  - `struct pss_store { root_fd, clips_dir_fd; struct seglog events, stats; next_event_id; boot_no; recovered; }`.
  - `store_open()`: mkdir events/, stats/, clips/; recover both logs (existing
    `store_valid_prefix` + truncate logic, run per log); scan events for ids,
    boots and dangling opens; append an interrupted close for each dangling
    open and `fdatasync`; prune old stats segments; existing tmp-clip cleanup
    and clip max-id.
  - `store_scan(root, which, fn, arg)` with `which` = `PSS_LOG_EVENTS` or `PSS_LOG_STATS`.
- **Records** (events log): `BOOT` (1), `EVENT` (2) = the complete/closing
  record (unchanged struct), new `EVENT_OPEN` (4) = `{event_id, start_mono_ns,
  start_wall_ns, kind, flags}`. New flag `PSS_EVF_INTERRUPTED`. Interrupted
  close: `end_mono_ns = start_mono_ns` (duration unknown) + flag.
  `STATS` (3) moves to the stats log only.
- **API for ENTRY (used by fusion in M4):** `store_event_open(s, &open_rec)`
  (append + fdatasync) and `store_event_close(s, &event_rec)` (append + fdatasync).
  `store_append_stats()` + `store_sync_stats()`.
- **Stats pruning:** `stats_prune(s, now)` at open and after each stats-segment
  rollover: delete non-newest `stats/seg-*.pel` whose mtime is > 7 days old,
  fsync the dir, log each.
- **`src/hub/hub.c`** (shared): boot → events log; `close_event` →
  `store_event_close`; `write_stats` → stats log. No behavior change.
- **`src/cli/pss.c`** (shared): scan events log; `--all` adds the stats log;
  show `interrupted (power lost)` for that flag and `IN PROGRESS` for an open
  with no close yet.
- Drop the unused `state/` dir (not in DESIGN.md's layout).
- **Docs:** M3-Status.md and source comments `Design.md` → `DESIGN.md`;
  M3-Status layout line updated.

## Tests (tests/test_store.c, test_e2e.c)
Existing tests keep their assertions, with paths `log/` → `events/`. New:
- stats records land in `stats/`, not `events/`; both logs recover a torn tail.
- open without close → reopen yields one EVENT with `PSS_EVF_INTERRUPTED`;
  reopening again does not add a second one.
- open + close → no interrupted record.
- stats prune: backdate a non-newest segment (utimensat) → deleted; newest kept.
- e2e: event record found via the events log; stats log exists.

## Verification
`make && make test && make asan && make netcheck` (CLAUDE.md DONE rule), plus
`make memcheck`; show output. Commit `M3: store split into events/stats logs,
ENTRY open records, interrupted recovery` only when asked.
Note for the Pi: no hub has run there yet, so there is no old `log/` data to migrate.

# M3 plan: PIR + camera through the real pipeline into real storage

## Context
Milestone 3 checkpoint demo: "both sensors flowing through the real pipeline into
real storage; at least one menu mechanism working; transcripts copied out."
The repo has only docs (Design.md, Problem-Memo.md, CLAUDE.md), no code yet.
The team has the **PIR and camera** now; the Snowball mic has not arrived. So the
M3 demo pair is **PIR + camera**. `micd` is written and unit-tested off-device but
**not** hardware-tested today. Session: Bryan, with edits authorized in all areas.

Demo story: wave at the PIR → `pird` gets a GPIO edge interrupt (mechanism B) →
`hub` writes an event record to the CRC-framed log (mechanism D) and tells `camd`
to shoot a burst → JPEGs are committed atomically into `clips/` and the event
record references them → `pss events` shows it from disk. Then pull the power
and show recovery on restart (D).

## Environment facts (checked)
- Lab machine: gcc 11.5, clang, valgrind, ALSA headers present; **no libgpiod**,
  no aarch64 cross compiler.
- Therefore: `make` / `make test` / `make asan` run on the lab machine for
  everything except linking `pird` against libgpiod; the Makefile builds `pird`
  only when `pkg-config libgpiod` succeeds. `make deploy PI=pi@host` rsyncs the
  tree to the Pi and runs `make` there (native build, libgpiod v2 + ALSA on Pi).
- All PIR logic that doesn't touch libgpiod (debounce, warm-up, msg encoding)
  lives in a pure-C file that is unit-tested on the lab machine.

## Files to create (layout from Design.md §12)
- `Makefile`: `all test asan memcheck netcheck deploy clean`; C17,
  `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wvla`. `netcheck` greps `src/` per Design §11.
- `src/common/`: `ipc.{c,h}` (AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET helpers, message structs:
  PIR edge, cam trigger, cam frame-ready, mic feature frame, heartbeat),
  `log.{c,h}` (timestamped stderr logging), `time.{c,h}` (mono + wall).
- `src/store/`: `log.{c,h}` (segment files `seg-NNNNNN.pel`, record framing
  `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]`, append, `fdatasync` on event
  close, 4 MB rollover), `recover.c` (scan newest segment, truncate at first bad
  len/CRC, delete `clips/*.tmp`, log the result), `clip.{c,h}` (tmp dir → fsync
  files → rename → fsync dir), `crc32.c`. Quota/eviction: simple oldest-first
  with the 5% floor (small, and it's part of D).
- `src/capture/pir/`: `pird.c` (libgpiod v2 line request, both edges, pull-up,
  kernel monotonic timestamps; `--poll=<ms>` via timerfd as comparison arm),
  `pir_logic.{c,h}` (debounce, 60 s warm-up ignore).
- `src/capture/cam/camd.c`: on trigger, fork/exec `rpicam-still` (timelapse
  burst ~2 fps × 10 s) into `clips/<id>.dir.tmp`, report frame-ready/done or
  failure (`no-images`). Binary path overridable by env for tests.
- `src/capture/mic/`: `micd.c` (ALSA capture thread + feature thread, SPSC ring,
  `-ENODEV` → exit 3, xrun → `snd_pcm_prepare`), `features.{c,h}` (radix-2 FFT,
  Hann window, RMS, 8 log bands, spectral flux). **Not hardware-tested at M3.**
- `src/hub/hub.c`: epoll loop over child sockets + signalfd + timerfd; writes
  `boot` record at start; PIR rise → open event + trigger camd; burst done →
  commit clip, then write event record referencing it; mic frames accepted and
  counted when present (no fusion yet).
- `src/cli/pss.c`: `pss events` reads the log segments read-only through the
  store API (query socket and `timeline`/`status`/`health` come later).
- `tests/`: `test_store.c` (append/read, torn-tail truncation, bad CRC, `.tmp`
  cleanup, clip commit), `test_ipc.c`, `test_pir_logic.c`, `test_features.c`
  (synthetic sine → expected band; silence → zero flux), `test_camd.c` (fake
  `rpicam-still` script writes dummy JPEGs; also failure exit path).
- `deploy/run-m3.sh`: starts hub, pird, camd (and micd if `--mic`) for the demo.

- Fusion FSM / detectors / background model (needs mic + collected data, M4).
  Consequence: at M3 every PIR burst is kept; Design's "delete unconfirmed
  bursts" applies once fusion exists. Stated in the M3 note.
- Supervisor (E) and `make soakcheck`: come next; `make soakcheck` will be added
  with the supervisor, not stubbed.

1. Makefile + common/ + crc32 + store log/recover + tests.
2. Clip commit + quota + tests.
3. pir_logic + pird + tests (pird builds on Pi only).
4. camd + fake-rpicam test.
5. hub wiring + `pss events`; end-to-end test on lab machine with a
   test-only PIR-edge injector over the socket (labelled as such; demo is live).
6. micd + features + tests.
7. run-m3.sh, M3 note (PIR+camera substitution, mic status), copy transcripts
   into `CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/bryan-rosas/`.
Commits only when Bryan asks, format `M3: <what>`.

- Lab machine: `make && make test && make asan && make netcheck`; `make memcheck`.

# Plan: bring src/store in line with Owen's updated DESIGN.md §5

## Context
M3 code is on `main` (3e87ee9). Owen's M2 revision (6fd043f) changed the
storage design after our store was written. Hardware testing is blocked
(no PIR jumper wires), so we use the time on Bryan's own area, `src/store`,
so it matches what graders will compare against. Session owner: Bryan.
`src/hub` and `src/cli` are shared; they get only the call-site changes the
new store API forces (covered by approving this plan).

What DESIGN.md §5 now requires that we don't do:
1. **Two logs:** `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel` and `stats/seg-NNNNNN.pel` (4 MB
   segments each, same framing), not one `log/`. Layout `{events, stats, clips}`.
2. **ENTRY durable at open:** `event_open` record + `fdatasync` when an ENTRY is
   confirmed; close record synced at end. MOTION_ONLY / SOUND_ONLY are written
   once, at close (what the hub does today, so M3 behavior is unchanged).
3. **Recovery closes dangling opens** as `interrupted (power lost)`.
4. **Stats retention:** whole stats segments deleted after 7 days.
5. Recovery truncates the newest segment of **both** logs.

## Design
- **`src/store/evlog.{c,h}`** becomes a generic segment log plus the store:
  - `struct seglog { int dir_fd, seg_fd; uint32_t seg_no; uint64_t seg_size; uint8_t buf[...]; }`
    with `seglog_append()` / `seglog_sync()`: the current append/rollover/
    truncate-on-failed-write code moved, not rewritten.
  - `struct pss_store { root_fd, clips_dir_fd; struct seglog events, stats; next_event_id; boot_no; recovered; }`.
  - `store_open()`: mkdir events/, stats/, clips/; recover both logs (existing
    `store_valid_prefix` + truncate logic, run per log); scan events for ids,
    boots and dangling opens; append an interrupted close for each dangling
    open and `fdatasync`; prune old stats segments; existing tmp-clip cleanup
    and clip max-id.
  - `store_scan(root, which, fn, arg)` with `which` = `PSS_LOG_EVENTS` or `PSS_LOG_STATS`.
- **Records** (events log): `BOOT` (1), `EVENT` (2) = the complete/closing
  record (unchanged struct), new `EVENT_OPEN` (4) = `{event_id, start_mono_ns,
  start_wall_ns, kind, flags}`. New flag `PSS_EVF_INTERRUPTED`. Interrupted
  close: `end_mono_ns = start_mono_ns` (duration unknown) + flag.
  `STATS` (3) moves to the stats log only.
- **API for ENTRY (used by fusion in M4):** `store_event_open(s, &open_rec)`
  (append + fdatasync) and `store_event_close(s, &event_rec)` (append + fdatasync).
  `store_append_stats()` + `store_sync_stats()`.
- **Stats pruning:** `stats_prune(s, now)` at open and after each stats-segment
  rollover: delete non-newest `stats/seg-*.pel` whose mtime is > 7 days old,
  fsync the dir, log each.
- **`src/hub/hub.c`** (shared): boot → events log; `close_event` →
  `store_event_close`; `write_stats` → stats log. No behavior change.
- **`src/cli/pss.c`** (shared): scan events log; `--all` adds the stats log;
  show `interrupted (power lost)` for that flag and `IN PROGRESS` for an open
  with no close yet.
- Drop the unused `state/` dir (not in DESIGN.md's layout).
- **Docs:** M3-Status.md and source comments `Design.md` → `DESIGN.md`;
  M3-Status layout line updated.

## Tests (tests/test_store.c, test_e2e.c)
Existing tests keep their assertions, with paths `log/` → `events/`. New:
- stats records land in `stats/`, not `events/`; both logs recover a torn tail.
- open without close → reopen yields one EVENT with `PSS_EVF_INTERRUPTED`;
  reopening again does not add a second one.
- open + close → no interrupted record.
- stats prune: backdate a non-newest segment (utimensat) → deleted; newest kept.
- e2e: event record found via the events log; stats log exists.

## Verification
`make && make test && make asan && make netcheck` (CLAUDE.md DONE rule), plus
`make memcheck`; show output. Commit `M3: store split into events/stats logs,
ENTRY open records, interrupted recovery` only when asked.
Note for the Pi: no hub has run there yet, so there is no old `log/` data to migrate.

# M3 Status: Checkpoint Demo (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)

**Milestone requirement:** both sensors flowing through the real pipeline into
real storage; at least one menu mechanism working; transcripts copied out.

## Sensor substitution for this checkpoint
The Blue Snowball microphone has **not arrived yet**. The M3 demo therefore
uses the **PIR (HC-SR501) and the camera (Arducam OV5647)** as its two
sensors. `micd` is written and its feature extraction is unit-tested on
synthetic signals, but it has **not been run on real microphone hardware**.
Fusion of PIR and audio (DESIGN.md Section 4) needs the mic and data we collect, so
it is planned for M4. Until then, every PIR-triggered event is recorded as
`MOTION_ONLY` and tagged `audio-offline`, and every successful camera burst is
kept. (Once fusion exists, DESIGN.md Section 5 deletes unconfirmed bursts.)

## What the demo shows
```
wave at PIR -> pird (GPIO edge interrupt, B) -> hub -> event opened
                                              -> camd -> rpicam-still burst -> clips/<id>.dir.tmp
            hub commits the burst atomically (fsync, rename, fsync dir; D) -> clips/<id>.dir
            hub writes a CRC-framed event record + fdatasync (D) -> log/seg-000001.pel
pss events  -> reads the record back from disk
```
- **Mechanism B (interrupt-driven input):** `pird` blocks until the kernel
  delivers a GPIO edge with a CLOCK_MONOTONIC timestamp, and logs the
  edge-to-userspace latency per edge. `--poll=<ms>` is the polling arm for
  the head-to-head comparison.
- **Mechanism D (storage layer):** append-only CRC32-framed log with
  torn-tail recovery at startup; atomic clip commit; deletion of `*.tmp`
  left by interrupted writes; oldest-first quota with a free-space floor.
  Power-pull demo: pull the plug mid-burst, boot, and restart. The hub logs
  `store: recovered seg=N valid=R truncated_bytes=B` and removes the
  interrupted clip.

## Running it on the Pi
```
make deploy PI=pi@<host>          # copy the tree and build natively (needs libgpiod >= 2, ALSA)
ssh pi@<host>
cd pss && deploy/run-m3.sh        # hub + camd + pird; add --line=N if the PIR is not on GPIO17
build/pss events                  # in another terminal: what has been stored
```
Check the GPIO chip and line first with `gpioinfo`. Depending on the kernel,
the Pi 5 header is `gpiochip0` or `gpiochip4`; pass `--chip=` to override.
The PIR ignores edges for its first 60 s (sensor warm-up); `--warmup=0` skips
this for a quick check.

## Not in M3 (next milestones)
- Fusion FSM, detectors, background model (M4, needs the mic).
- Supervisor (mechanism E) and `make soakcheck`.
- Hub query socket; `pss timeline / status / health / expect / settime`.

## Verification on the lab machine
`make`, `make test`, `make asan` (clang ASan+UBSan), `make memcheck`
(valgrind) and `make netcheck` all pass. `pird` cannot link on the lab
machines (no libgpiod), so it builds on the Pi. It was compile-checked
against the libgpiod v2.1 header. `tests/test_e2e` runs the real hub and camd
with a stand-in camera script, with the test itself sending PIR edges in

# M3 Status: Checkpoint Demo (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)

**Milestone requirement:** both sensors flowing through the real pipeline into
real storage; at least one menu mechanism working; transcripts copied out.

## Sensor substitution for this checkpoint
The Blue Snowball microphone has **not arrived yet**. The M3 demo therefore
uses the **PIR (HC-SR501) and the camera (Arducam OV5647)** as its two
sensors. `micd` is written and its feature extraction is unit-tested on
synthetic signals, but it has **not been run on real microphone hardware**.
Fusion of PIR and audio (DESIGN.md Section 4) needs the mic and data we collect, so
it is planned for M4. Until then, every PIR-triggered event is recorded as
`MOTION_ONLY` and tagged `audio-offline`, and every successful camera burst is
kept. (Once fusion exists, DESIGN.md Section 5 deletes unconfirmed bursts.)

## What the demo shows
```
wave at PIR -> pird (GPIO edge interrupt, B) -> hub -> event opened
                                              -> camd -> rpicam-still burst -> clips/<id>.dir.tmp
            hub commits the burst atomically (fsync, rename, fsync dir; D) -> clips/<id>.dir
            hub writes a CRC-framed event record + fdatasync (D) -> events/seg-NNNNNN.pel
            (per-minute stats go to a separate log, stats/seg-NNNNNN.pel)
pss events  -> reads the record back from disk
```
- **Mechanism B (interrupt-driven input):** `pird` blocks until the kernel
  delivers a GPIO edge with a CLOCK_MONOTONIC timestamp, and logs the
  edge-to-userspace latency per edge. `--poll=<ms>` is the polling arm for
  the head-to-head comparison.
- **Mechanism D (storage layer):** append-only CRC32-framed log with
  torn-tail recovery at startup; atomic clip commit; deletion of `*.tmp`
  left by interrupted writes; oldest-first quota with a free-space floor.
  Power-pull demo: pull the plug mid-burst, boot, and restart. The hub logs
  `store: recovered seg=N valid=R truncated_bytes=B` and removes the
  interrupted clip.

## Running it on the Pi
```
make deploy PI=pi@<host>          # copy the tree and build natively (needs libgpiod >= 2, ALSA)
ssh pi@<host>
cd pss && deploy/run-m3.sh        # hub + camd + pird; add --line=N if the PIR is not on GPIO17
build/pss events                  # in another terminal: what has been stored
```
Check the GPIO chip and line first with `gpioinfo`. Depending on the kernel,
the Pi 5 header is `gpiochip0` or `gpiochip4`; pass `--chip=` to override.
The PIR ignores edges for its first 60 s (sensor warm-up); `--warmup=0` skips
this for a quick check.

## Not in M3 (next milestones)
- Fusion FSM, detectors, background model (M4, needs the mic).
- Supervisor (mechanism E) and `make soakcheck`.
- Hub query socket; `pss timeline / status / health / expect / settime`.

## Verification on the lab machine
`make`, `make test`, `make asan` (clang ASan+UBSan), `make memcheck`
(valgrind) and `make netcheck` all pass. `pird` cannot link on the lab
machines (no libgpiod), so it builds on the Pi. It was compile-checked
against the libgpiod v2.1 header. `tests/test_e2e` runs the real hub and camd
with a stand-in camera script, with the test itself sending PIR edges in
place of `pird`. **Not yet verified on the Pi:** `pird` with the real PIR,
`rpicam-still` burst arguments, and `micd` (no microphone yet).

content.text:
The storage layer now matches DESIGN.md Section 5. Build, test, asan, memcheck and netcheck all pass, and `pird` still compiles against the libgpiod v2 header.

**What changed in `src/store` (your area):**
- **Two logs:** events go to `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel` and per-minute stats to `stats/seg-NNNNNN.pel`. There's no `log/` or `state/` directory any more. Recovery cuts off a damaged last record in both logs.
- **ENTRY saved the moment it opens:** `store_event_open()` writes and syncs an open record right away, and `store_event_close()` syncs the close. Nothing calls these yet, because ENTRY events need fusion (M4); MOTION_ONLY events are still written once, when they close.
- **Interrupted entries:** on restart, an entry that was opened but never closed gets closed and marked `interrupted (power lost)`. Any photos already saved for it are kept. It happens only once, not again on later restarts.
- **7-day stats retention:** old stats files are deleted whole once they're more than 7 days old.

**One addition beyond the plan:** at about one record per minute, a 4 MB stats file would take roughly 40 days to fill, so nothing would ever be old enough to delete after 7 days. The stats log now starts a fresh file at every boot and every 24 hours, so old ones can actually age out.

**Shared code** (only the changes the new store required):
- **[hub.c](src/hub/hub.c):** writes boot records and events to the events log and stats to the stats log. It behaves the same otherwise.
- **[pss.c](src/cli/pss.c):** shows `[interrupted (power lost)]` and `IN PROGRESS` entries. `--all` adds the stats records.

**Comment-only changes in Owen's files:** the `Design.md` → `DESIGN.md` and "§" → "Section" fixes also edited comments in `src/capture/`. No code there changed.

**Tests:** the existing store tests keep their checks, now pointed at `events/` (the rollover test uses `stats/`). There are 5 new tests:
- stats kept separate from events, and stats recovery
- interrupted-entry recovery, including that it happens only once
- an entry that opens and closes normally isn't marked interrupted
- deleting stats older than 7 days
- the 24-hour stats rollover

The end-to-end test also checks that both logs exist.

content.text:
The store update is on `main` as `14c331a`. I checked GitHub first; nobody else had pushed, so it went straight on top of the M3 commit. All checks passed before the commit.

Owen will get the new layout on their next `git pull`. If you've already cloned on the Pi, run `git pull` there too.

**What's left for M3:**
1. **Wire the PIR** when you have the jumper wires; the wiring steps from before still apply.
2. **Run the full demo on the Pi:** PIR → hub → camera → `pss events`, plus the power-pull test.
3. **Wrap up:** update M3-Status.md with what actually worked on the Pi, and copy this session's transcript into `CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/bryan-rosas/`.

Until the wires arrive, you could test the camera through the pipeline with a small stand-in that pretends to be the PIR.
alright, we don't have wires. change of plans. our two sensors are going to be the camera and the mic, is that possible?

lastPrompt: alright, we don't have wires. change of plans. our two sensors are going to be the camera and the mic, is that possible?

content.text:
Yes, that's possible, and it might be the quicker route. A USB mic needs no wires: you plug it in. A few things change, though.

**How the demo would work:** a sound (door slam, clap, voice) → `micd` detects a sudden jump in loudness against the room's background → the hub opens an event → `camd` takes a burst → everything is saved → `pss events` shows it. Today the hub only opens events on PIR signals, so it would need a sound trigger added.

**What this changes:**
1. **The hub needs a sound trigger.** It's a small detector: open an event when the sound jump is well above the recent background. That's an algorithm change in shared code, so under CLAUDE.md I'd plan it first and wait for your OK.
2. **Mechanism B drops out of the demo.** B is the PIR's GPIO interrupt, and the arm button also needs wires. D (storage) still works and is tested, and M3 only needs one working mechanism, so you're still covered.
3. **`micd` has never run on a real mic.** That's now the biggest risk, so the first step is checking the mic on the Pi before any code changes.
4. **It's a checkpoint substitution, not a design change.** The final design stays PIR + mic. I'd note the swap in M3-Status.md, and Owen should know, since `micd` is in their area.

**Do you have the Blue Snowball now?** If yes, first plug it into the Pi and run these in the Pi's terminal:
```
arecord -l
arecord -D plughw:CARD=Snowball -f S16_LE -r 44100 -c 1 -d 5 test.wav
aplay test.wav
```
Tell me whether `arecord -l` lists a card, and what its name is, and whether you heard yourself on playback. Then I'll plan the sound trigger.
i do not have the blue snowball now, is that the next step? get it, plug it in and run those commands?

Yes. Whichever sensor you choose, the next step is getting the hardware and plugging it in. But compare the two paths first, because one is clearly easier:

| | **PIR + camera** (original plan) | **Mic + camera** (new idea) |
|---|---|---|
| What you need | 3 female-to-female jumper wires (a few dollars, often free at a campus makerspace or electronics lab) | A USB microphone |
| Code | **Already done** | Needs a new sound trigger in the hub (plan, write, test) |
| Matches DESIGN.md | Yes | No, it's a substitution you'd have to explain |
| Mechanism B in the demo | Yes | No (D only) |

**My recommendation:** get jumper wires and stick with PIR + camera. The code is written and tested, and it's the design the graders have.

**If the mic is easier to get:** it doesn't have to be the Snowball. Any USB mic works for this, including a USB headset or a webcam with a built-in mic. Plug it into the Pi and run the `arecord` commands, swapping `Snowball` for whatever name `arecord -l` shows.

Either way, tell me when you have one in hand and we'll take it from there.
we're gonna get the mic, pls hold

lastPrompt: we're gonna get the mic, pls hold

content.text:
Okay, I'll wait. When you have the mic:

1. Plug it into any USB port on the Pi.
2. In the Pi's terminal:
   ```
   arecord -l
   arecord -D plughw:CARD=<name> -f S16_LE -r 44100 -c 1 -d 5 test.wav
   aplay test.wav
   ```
   Replace `<name>` with the card name `arecord -l` shows (e.g. `Snowball`).
3. Tell me the card name and whether you heard your recording.

Then I'll plan the sound trigger for the hub.
ok will this thread be here when i get back?

Yes. This conversation is saved, and you can pick it up again later.

- **In VS Code:** open the Claude Code panel and find this conversation in the past-conversations list (the history/clock icon at the top of the panel). Open it and keep typing; I'll have everything we've done.
- **From a terminal:** `claude --resume` in the project folder lets you choose this session from a list.

If you start a **new** conversation instead, I won't remember this one. Everything important is in the repo, though: the code, [M3-Status.md](M3-Status.md), and the commits on `main`. A new session could pick up from there if you tell it "we're doing the mic + camera substitution for M3, next step is the sound trigger in the hub."

**One reminder for the end:** this session's transcript file keeps growing, so when you finish M3, copy the final version into `CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/bryan-rosas/` again.

# Plan: bring src/store in line with Owen's updated DESIGN.md Section 5

## Context
M3 code is on `main` (3e87ee9). Owen's M2 revision (6fd043f) changed the
storage design after our store was written. Hardware testing is blocked
(no PIR jumper wires), so we use the time on Bryan's own area, `src/store`,
so it matches what graders will compare against. Session owner: Bryan.
`src/hub` and `src/cli` are shared; they get only the call-site changes the
new store API forces (covered by approving this plan).

What DESIGN.md Section 5 now requires that we don't do:
1. **Two logs:** `events/seg-NNNNNN.pel` and `stats/seg-NNNNNN.pel` (4 MB
   segments each, same framing), not one `log/`. Layout `{events, stats, clips}`.
2. **ENTRY durable at open:** `event_open` record + `fdatasync` when an ENTRY is
   confirmed; close record synced at end. MOTION_ONLY / SOUND_ONLY are written
   once, at close (what the hub does today, so M3 behavior is unchanged).
3. **Recovery closes dangling opens** as `interrupted (power lost)`.
4. **Stats retention:** whole stats segments deleted after 7 days.
5. Recovery truncates the newest segment of **both** logs.

## Design
- **`src/store/evlog.{c,h}`** becomes a generic segment log plus the store:
  - `struct seglog { int dir_fd, seg_fd; uint32_t seg_no; uint64_t seg_size; uint8_t buf[...]; }`
    with `seglog_append()` / `seglog_sync()`: the current append/rollover/
    truncate-on-failed-write code moved, not rewritten.
  - `struct pss_store { root_fd, clips_dir_fd; struct seglog events, stats; next_event_id; boot_no; recovered; }`.
  - `store_open()`: mkdir events/, stats/, clips/; recover both logs (existing
    `store_valid_prefix` + truncate logic, run per log); scan events for ids,
    boots and dangling opens; append an interrupted close for each dangling
    open and `fdatasync`; prune old stats segments; existing tmp-clip cleanup
    and clip max-id.
  - `store_scan(root, which, fn, arg)` with `which` = `PSS_LOG_EVENTS` or `PSS_LOG_STATS`.
- **Records** (events log): `BOOT` (1), `EVENT` (2) = the complete/closing
  record (unchanged struct), new `EVENT_OPEN` (4) = `{event_id, start_mono_ns,
  start_wall_ns, kind, flags}`. New flag `PSS_EVF_INTERRUPTED`. Interrupted
  close: `end_mono_ns = start_mono_ns` (duration unknown) + flag.
  `STATS` (3) moves to the stats log only.
- **API for ENTRY (used by fusion in M4):** `store_event_open(s, &open_rec)`
  (append + fdatasync) and `store_event_close(s, &event_rec)` (append + fdatasync).
  `store_append_stats()` + `store_sync_stats()`.
- **Stats pruning:** `stats_prune(s, now)` at open and after each stats-segment
  rollover: delete non-newest `stats/seg-*.pel` whose mtime is > 7 days old,
  fsync the dir, log each.
- **`src/hub/hub.c`** (shared): boot → events log; `close_event` →
  `store_event_close`; `write_stats` → stats log. No behavior change.
- **`src/cli/pss.c`** (shared): scan events log; `--all` adds the stats log;
  show `interrupted (power lost)` for that flag and `IN PROGRESS` for an open
  with no close yet.
- Drop the unused `state/` dir (not in DESIGN.md's layout).
- **Docs:** M3-Status.md and source comments `Design.md` → `DESIGN.md`, and
  every "§N" → "Section N" (Bryan's preference); M3-Status layout line updated.

## Tests (tests/test_store.c, test_e2e.c)
Existing tests keep their assertions, with paths `log/` → `events/`. New:
- stats records land in `stats/`, not `events/`; both logs recover a torn tail.
- open without close → reopen yields one EVENT with `PSS_EVF_INTERRUPTED`;
  reopening again does not add a second one.
- open + close → no interrupted record.
- stats prune: backdate a non-newest segment (utimensat) → deleted; newest kept.
- e2e: event record found via the events log; stats log exists.

## Verification
`make && make test && make asan && make netcheck` (CLAUDE.md DONE rule), plus
`make memcheck`; show output. Commit `M3: store split into events/stats logs,
ENTRY open records, interrupted recovery` only when asked.
Note for the Pi: no hub has run there yet, so there is no old `log/` data to migrate.

# Portable Security System: team rules

## Commands
- Build: `make`    Cross/deploy: `make deploy PI=pi@<host>`
- Tests: `make test`    Sanitizers: `make asan`    Valgrind: `make memcheck`
- Network boundary check: `make netcheck` (fails if network code appears
  outside the hotspot UI server; see DESIGN.md Section 11)
- Soak sanity: `make soakcheck` (1-hour miniature of the 48h run)
- A change is DONE only when build, test, asan, and netcheck pass. Show output.

## Hard constraints
- The PRODUCT makes no network calls. Its only network code is the
  local UI server, bound to the Pi's own hotspot address (no internet
  uplink, no outbound connections). No LLM APIs, no cloud inference,
  no pretrained models. The intelligence in src/analysis is ours.
  This is a graded boundary.
- Every daemon must be supervisable: clean exit codes, no orphaned
  fds across restart, heartbeat within 60s of start.
- Every allocation checked; every syscall's error path handled and
  logged. The 48-hour soak is the test suite of last resort.
- NEVER weaken, skip, or delete a test to make the suite pass.

## Project facts (see DESIGN.md)
- Pi 5, wall powered (no battery). RTC backup battery is required: wall
  time across power cuts depends on it.
- Sensors: HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO), Blue Snowball USB mic (ALSA), OV5647
  camera (CSI, evidence only), arm button + LED (GPIO).
- Safe to hot-unplug for fault injection: the USB mic. The PIR only via
  its keyed connector. NEVER hot-unplug the CSI camera ribbon.

## Ownership
- Owen: capture daemons and arm button (src/capture/{pir,mic,cam})
- Bryan: storage layer, analysis engine (src/store, src/analysis)
- Shared: hub, supervisor, CLI, UI (src/hub, src/supervisor, src/cli, ui/)
- Each partner works in their own clone and their own Claude Code
  sessions; never prompt jointly in one session. Copy transcripts to
  CLAUDE-TRANSCRIPTS/<name>/ at every milestone.
- The agent edits outside the session owner's area only when told
  explicitly to.

## Style
- Systems core: C17, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, no VLAs.
  goto-cleanup for multi-resource functions.
- Python permitted only under tools/ and ui/. No graded mechanism
  may live there.
- Smallest diff that passes. Do not refactor unrelated code.

## Workflow
- Multi-file or algorithmic change: plan first, wait for approval.
- Hardware bugs: paste real evidence (dmesg, timing capture,
  /proc/interrupts). No fixes proposed from a verbal description.
- Commit only from a green state; message format "M<n>: <what>".
- [No section sign](no-section-sign.md) — write "Section N", never the "§" symbol

<tools-used-before-summary>AskUserQuestion, Bash, Edit, ExitPlanMode, Read, ToolSearch, Write</tools-used-before-summary>
Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Bryan Rosas (CSU CS370, teammate Owen Pendleton) is working on Milestone 3 of the "Portable Security System" term project: "Checkpoint demo: both sensors flowing through the real pipeline into real storage; at least one menu mechanism working; transcripts copied out."
   - He first wanted explanations, then working code for M3. He authorized edits in all areas for M3. Original demo pair: PIR + camera, with mic code written but not hardware-tested.
   - Later requests:
     - commit and push (to main, after Owen OK'd: "owen said it's fine, push omg")
     - Pi setup instructions on monitor and keyboard, step by step
     - bring the storage layer in line with Owen's updated DESIGN.md Section 5
     - stop using the "§" character
   - Change of plan: the demo sensors become camera + mic (no PIR wires). The mic hasn't arrived; Bryan said "pls hold."
   - Owen's Claude will build the mic-triggers-camera piece. Bryan asked for a handoff prompt for Owen's Claude (given).
   - Most recent request: "update my transcripts". Done and pushed.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Raspberry Pi 5 sensors: HC-SR501 PIR (GPIO), USB mic (ALSA), OV5647 camera (CSI, `rpicam-still`), and an arm button + LED (in Owen's new design).
   - Mechanisms from the course menu: B (interrupt-driven GPIO input via libgpiod v2 edge events with kernel CLOCK_MONOTONIC timestamps, vs `--poll` with a timerfd), D (crash-consistent storage), E (supervisor; not built yet).
   - IPC: AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET with a fixed-size `struct pss_msg`, HELLO/heartbeat every 5 s, client reconnect with backoff.
   - Storage:
     - CRC32-framed records `[len u32][type u16][ver u16][payload][crc32]`.
     - 4 MB segments; torn-tail truncation on recovery.
     - Atomic clip commit: tmp dir → fsync files → fsync dir → rename → fsync clips/.
     - Oldest-first quota with a 5% free-space floor.
     - Separate events/ and stats/ logs; EVENT_OPEN records synced immediately.
     - Interrupted-entry recovery.
     - Stats segments rolled per boot and every 24 h; whole segments deleted after 7 days.
   - Audio features: 1024-pt Hann window, 882-sample hop, our own radix-2 FFT, 8 log bands 100 Hz–8 kHz, spectral flux.
   - Code style: C17, `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wvla`, goto-cleanup, signalfd/timerfd/epoll.
   - Build: Makefile targets all/test/asan (clang on lab machines)/memcheck/netcheck/deploy/clean. pird builds only where libgpiod ≥ 2.0 exists (the Pi).

3. Files and Code Sections (all in /s/bach/l/under/C836990995/cs370/termProject/Portable-Security-System):
   - **Makefile**:
     - Objects in `$(BUILD)/obj/`; binaries `$(BUILD)/{hub,camd,pss,pird,micd}`; test binaries in `$(BUILD)/tests/`.
     - `HAVE_GPIOD` / `HAVE_ALSA` detected via pkg-config.
     - `ASAN_CC := $(shell command -v clang ... || echo $(CC))`; `asan:` runs `$(MAKE) CC=$(ASAN_CC) BUILD=build-asan SAN="-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fno-sanitize-recover=all" test`.
     - `TEST_ENV := PSS_BIN_DIR=$(abspath $(BUILD)) PSS_TEST_DIR=$(CURDIR)/tests`.
     - netcheck greps src/ for AF_INET, getaddrinfo, gethostbyname, curl, `https?:`, and `connect(` outside src/common/ipc.c.
     - `deploy` uses rsync + ssh.
   - **compile_flags.txt** (for clangd), **.gitignore** (build/, build-asan/).
   - **src/common/**:
     - log.{c,h}: `pss_log_init`, `pss_log`; one write() per line; the placeholder "(no clock)" replaced a trigraph.
     - time.{c,h}: `PSS_NS_PER_MS INT64_C(1000000)`, `PSS_NS_PER_S INT64_C(1000000000)`, `pss_mono_ns`, `pss_wall_ns`.
     - util.{c,h}: `pss_run_dir` (PSS_RUN_DIR, default /run/pss), `pss_data_dir` (PSS_DATA_DIR, default /var/lib/pss), `pss_parse_u32`, `pss_signalfd`, `pss_timerfd`, `pss_timerfd_drain`.
     - ipc.{c,h}: roles PIR=1/CAM=2/MIC=3; message types HELLO, HEARTBEAT, PIR_EDGE, CAM_TRIGGER, CAM_DONE, MIC_FRAME; `PSS_NBANDS 8`; functions `pss_msg_init`, `ipc_sock_path` (→ hub.sock), `ipc_listen`, `ipc_connect` (nonblocking), `ipc_send` (MSG_NOSIGNAL), `ipc_recv` (1/0/-1; EBADMSG, EPROTO).
     - client.{c,h}: `struct pss_client`; `client_init`, `client_poll_connect`, `client_send`, `client_disconnect`, `client_close`.
   - **src/store/**:
     - crc32.{c,h}
     - dirlist.{c,h}
     - clip.{c,h}: `clip_tmp_name`, `clip_final_name`, `clip_commit`, `clip_discard`, `clip_cleanup_tmp`, `clip_count_images` (added), `clip_max_id`, `clip_enforce_quota` (returns 0, 1 = floor reached, or -1).
     - evlog.{c,h}, rewritten for DESIGN.md Section 5:
       - Enums: `PSS_LOG_EVENTS` / `PSS_LOG_STATS`; record types BOOT=1, EVENT=2, STATS=3 (stats log only), EVENT_OPEN=4; flags NO_IMAGES, AUDIO_OFFLINE, CLOSED_AT_SHUTDOWN, INTERRUPTED (1<<3).
       - Structs: `struct pss_rec_event_open {event_id, start_mono_ns, start_wall_ns, kind, flags}`; `struct seglog {name, dir_fd, seg_fd, seg_no, seg_size, seg_started_ns, buf}`; `struct pss_store {root_fd, clips_dir_fd, events, stats, stats_roll_ns, next_event_id, boot_no, recovered}`; `struct store_recovery` (seg_no, valid_records, truncated_bytes, stats_seg_no, stats_valid_records, stats_truncated_bytes, stats_pruned, interrupted, tmp_removed).
       - API: `store_open`, `store_append(s, which, type, payload, len)` (rejects STATS outside the stats log and vice versa), `store_sync(s, which)`, `store_event_open`, `store_event_close`, `store_close`, `store_scan(root, which, fn, arg)`, `store_valid_prefix`.
       - `store_open`: recovers both logs, starts a fresh stats segment if the newest is non-empty, prunes stats older than 7 days, cleans tmp clips, closes dangling opens as INTERRUPTED (keeping committed image counts).
   - **src/capture/pir/**:
     - pir_logic.{c,h}: warm-up and duplicate filter.
     - pird.c: libgpiod v2, options `--chip=/dev/gpiochip0 --line=17 --poll=MS --warmup=SEC`; exit code 3 when the device is gone; logs `edge rise lat=...us`.
   - **src/capture/cam/camd.c**: runs `rpicam-still -n -t <frames*interval> --timelapse <interval> --width 1296 --height 972 -q 85 -o <clips>/<id>.dir.tmp/img%04d.jpg`. `PSS_RPICAM` overrides the binary. SIGCHLD reaping, deadline kill, kills a running burst at shutdown.
   - **src/capture/mic/**:
     - features.{c,h}: FFT, bands, flux.
     - micd.c: capture thread, SPSC ring of 2^19 samples, eventfd wake; `--device=default`; xrun recovery; exit 3 on ENODEV/EIO. Never run on real hardware.
   - **src/hub/hub.c**:
     - epoll over listen, signal, 1 s tick and connections.
     - Writes a BOOT record at start. PIR rise → `open_event` → `trigger_burst` (quota check, CAM_TRIGGER) → CAM_DONE → `clip_commit` → after quiet with no PIR high → `close_event` → `store_event_close`.
     - Stats written to the stats log every 60 s (first at 5 s), with an `hb:` log line.
     - Options: `--quiet-ms=30000 --burst-frames=20 --burst-interval-ms=500 --quota-mb=2048 --floor-pct=5`.
     - The `PSS_MSG_MIC_FRAME` case (~line 277) only counts frames.
   - **src/cli/pss.c**: `pss events [--all] [--data=DIR]`; shows interrupted / IN PROGRESS; `--all` scans the stats log.
   - **tests/**:
     - t.h (CHECK, T_RUN, T_END, t_mkdtemp, t_rm_rf)
     - test_store.c (14 tests)
     - test_ipc.c
     - test_pir_logic.c
     - test_features.c
     - test_e2e.c (real hub + camd with fake-rpicam-still.sh; the test plays pird; two sessions, success and FAKE_RPICAM_FAIL; checks the events/ and stats/ dirs)
     - fake-rpicam-still.sh (executable)
   - **deploy/run-m3.sh**: starts hub, camd, pird (plus micd with `--mic`); installs data/run dirs via sudo if needed.
   - **M3-Status.md**: grader note covering the substitution, the demo, the run steps, what is not done, and verification. Updated for events/stats and DESIGN.md naming. It does not yet reflect the mic+camera substitution.
   - Comment references changed from `Design.md` to `DESIGN.md` and from "§N" to "Section N" across src/ (including comment-only edits in Owen's capture files).
   - Memory: memory/no-section-sign.md and a MEMORY.md index line.
   - Plan file: /s/bach/l/under/C836990995/.claude/plans/this-is-the-second-cozy-pearl.md (latest version: the transcript-update plan).

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Trigraph `"????-??-??"` would be an error under -std=c17 -Werror → replaced with "(no clock)".
   - `-Wformat` mismatch (`long long` vs PRId64) → made the time constants INT64_C.
   - Linker error "cannot open output file build/hub: Is a directory" → objects moved under build/obj/; added mkdir -p to the test link rule.
   - test_e2e: missing `<inttypes.h>`; popen/ls hack replaced with opendir; the noisy initial scan is skipped if the data dir doesn't exist.
   - `make asan` failed ("cannot find libasan.so.6.0.0") → asan builds with clang when it's available.
   - A test-only compound-literal `strcat` was replaced with snprintf.
   - Push to main was rejected because Owen had pushed c6e2477/6fd043f → I stopped and surfaced the ownership and design changes; after Owen's OK, rebased and pushed.
   - User feedback: "stop using that weird character for 'section'" → I use "Section N" everywhere and saved it to memory.

5. Problem Solving:
   - pird can't link on the lab machine (no libgpiod) → syntax-checked against the downloaded libgpiod v2.1.3 header in the scratchpad (gpiod/gpiod.h).
   - Stats retention couldn't work with 4 MB segments at about 1 record/min → added a fresh stats segment per boot and a 24 h roll (`stats_roll_ns`).

# M3 Status: Checkpoint Demo (Owen Pendleton, Bryan Rosas)

**Milestone requirement:** both sensors flowing through the real pipeline into
real storage; at least one menu mechanism working; transcripts copied out.

## Sensor substitution for this checkpoint
The Blue Snowball microphone has **not arrived yet**. The M3 demo therefore
uses the **PIR (HC-SR501) and the camera (Arducam OV5647)** as its two
sensors. `micd` is written and its feature extraction is unit-tested on
synthetic signals, but it has **not been run on real microphone hardware**.
Fusion of PIR and audio (DESIGN.md Section 4) needs the mic and data we collect, so
it is planned for M4. Until then, every PIR-triggered event is recorded as
`MOTION_ONLY` and tagged `audio-offline`, and every successful camera burst is
kept. (Once fusion exists, DESIGN.md Section 5 deletes unconfirmed bursts.)

## What the demo shows
```
wave at PIR -> pird (GPIO edge interrupt, B) -> hub -> event opened
                                              -> camd -> rpicam-still burst -> clips/<id>.dir.tmp
            hub commits the burst atomically (fsync, rename, fsync dir; D) -> clips/<id>.dir
            hub writes a CRC-framed event record + fdatasync (D) -> events/seg-NNNNNN.pel
            (per-minute stats go to a separate log, stats/seg-NNNNNN.pel)
pss events  -> reads the record back from disk
```
- **Mechanism B (interrupt-driven input):** `pird` blocks until the kernel
  delivers a GPIO edge with a CLOCK_MONOTONIC timestamp, and logs the
  edge-to-userspace latency per edge. `--poll=<ms>` is the polling arm for
  the head-to-head comparison.
- **Mechanism D (storage layer):** separate append-only CRC32-framed event
  and stats logs with torn-tail recovery at startup; ENTRY records made
  durable when the entry opens, and any entry left open by a power cut
  closed as `interrupted (power lost)`; stats segments deleted whole after
  7 days; atomic clip commit; deletion of `*.tmp` left by interrupted
  writes; oldest-first clip quota with a free-space floor. Power-pull demo:
  pull the plug mid-burst, boot, and restart. The hub logs
  `store: recovered events seg=N valid=R truncated_bytes=B` and removes the
  interrupted clip. (ENTRY events themselves need fusion, M4; the store
  side is done and tested.)

## Running it on the Pi
```
make deploy PI=pi@<host>          # copy the tree and build natively (needs libgpiod >= 2, ALSA)
ssh pi@<host>
cd pss && deploy/run-m3.sh        # hub + camd + pird; add --line=N if the PIR is not on GPIO17
build/pss events                  # in another terminal: what has been stored
```
Check the GPIO chip and line first with `gpioinfo`. Depending on the kernel,
the Pi 5 header is `gpiochip0` or `gpiochip4`; pass `--chip=` to override.
The PIR ignores edges for its first 60 s (sensor warm-up); `--warmup=0` skips
this for a quick check.

## Not in M3 (next milestones)
- Fusion FSM, detectors, background model (M4, needs the mic).
- Supervisor (mechanism E) and `make soakcheck`.
- Hub query socket; `pss timeline / status / health / expect / settime`.

## Verification on the lab machine
`make`, `make test`, `make asan` (clang ASan+UBSan), `make memcheck`
(valgrind) and `make netcheck` all pass. `pird` cannot link on the lab
machines (no libgpiod), so it builds on the Pi. It was compile-checked
against the libgpiod v2.1 header. `tests/test_e2e` runs the real hub and camd
with a stand-in camera script, with the test itself sending PIR edges in
place of `pird`. **Not yet verified on the Pi:** `pird` with the real PIR,
`rpicam-still` burst arguments, and `micd` (no microphone yet).
